source_text: τῶν θείων κατεξανιστάμενοι νόμων, πυρεῖα προσῆγον ἄκλητοι καὶ αὐτόμολοι πρὸς τοῦτο ἰόντες, καὶ τιμὴν ἁρπάζοντες, οὐ νεμηθεῖσαν αὐτοῖς, ἀντιπαρεξάγοντες καὶ μάλα θερμῶς, τὰ ἐξ ἀπονοίας καὶ θράσους, ἱερεῖ τῷ προὔχοντι, καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ἁπάντων ἀπολέγδην ἐξῃρημένῳ. Ἐσκιαγραφεῖτο δὲ διὰ τούτων ἡ ἐσομένη κατὰ Χριστοῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων ἀπόνοια. Αὐτὸς γὰρ ἡμῶν ἀρχιερεὺς, ψήφῳ πρὸς τοῦτο ἠγμένος τῇ παρὰ Πατρὸς, καὶ οἱ μὲν τῶν οὕτως αἰσχρῶν ἐπιχειρημάτων ἐκτετίκασι δίκας· ἀποτίσουσι δὲ καὶ μετ' αὐτοὺς Ἰουδαῖοι τοῖς ἴσοις ἐγκλήμασι γεγονότες ἔνοχοι. Θεὸς δὲ δὴ τότε πρὸς Μωσέα τε τὸν ἱερὸν, καὶ μὴν καὶ πρὸς Ἐλεάζαρ ἔφη, τὸν ἐξ Ἀαρὼν τὸν ἱερέα· «Ἀνέλεσθε τὰ πυρεῖα τὰ χαλκᾶ ἐκ μέσου τῶν κεκαυμένων, καὶ τὸ πῦρ τὸ ἀλλότριον τοῦτο σπεῖρον ἐκεῖ, ὅτι ἡγίασε τὰ πυρεῖα τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν τούτων ἐν ταῖς ψυχαῖς αὐτῶν. Καὶ ἐποίησαν αὐτὰ λεπίδας ἐλατὰς, περίθεμα τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ, ὅτι προσηνέχθησαν ἔναντι Κυρίου, καὶ ἡγιάσθησαν. Καὶ ἐγένοντο εἰς σημεῖον τοῖς υἱοῖς Ἰσραήλ. «Ταύτῃ μὲν οὖν ἔφη τὸ τηνικάδε Θεός. Ἐν τῇ Ἐξόδῳ δὲ γέγραπται περὶ τοῦ Βεσελεὴλ, ὃς ἦν ἐκ πατρὸς μὲν Οὐρίου, φυλῆς δὲ τῆς Δὰν, καὶ πάσης εὐτεχνίας ἡγούμενος· «Οὗτος ἐποίησε τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ χαλκοῦν ἐκ τῶν πυρείων τῶν χαλκῶν, ἃ ἦν τοῖς ἀνδράσι τοῖς καταστασιάσασι μετὰ τῆς Κορὲ συναγωγῆς.» {ΠΑΛΛ.} Τί οὖν τοῦτό γε; {ΚΥΡ.} Πολλὴν ἂν ἔχοι τὴν ὄνησιν, εἰ ἐννοοῖτο ὅτι πεποίηται μὲν ἡ κιβωτὸς εἰς τύπον Χριστοῦ, καὶ μέν τοι καὶ τὰ ἕτερα, λυχνία, φημὶ, καὶ τὸ ἱλαστήριον, καὶ ἐκ χρυσίου τράπεζα, προσκομίσαντος τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ ἀναθέντος ἑκάστου τὸ ἐν χερσί. Δεκτοὶ γὰρ λίαν εἰς δόξαν Θεοῦ καὶ Πατρὸς, οἱ καρποφοροῦντες Χριστῷ, καὶ δωροφορίας προσάγοντες τὰς πνευματικὰς, ὧν ἦσαν ἐκεῖνοι τύποι καὶ σκιαί. Τῆς δὲ κατὰ νόμον λατρείας τὸ θυσιαστήριον, παροξυσμοῦ καὶ ἀντιλογίας, καὶ ἵν' οὕτως εἴπω λοιπὸν, ἀντάρσεως τῆς καθ' ἱερέως τοῦ μεγάλου γεγενημένης, οἱονεί πως ὑπόμνημα καὶ προαναφώνησις, ἐν αὐτῇ κειμένη τῇ κατασκευῇ, μυστικῶς τε καὶ οἰκονομικῶς σημαίνεται. Ἆρά σοι σαφὲς τὸ αἴνιγμα; Χριστοῦ γὰρ εἰς τύπον ὁ Ἀαρών· πεφιλονεικήκασι δὲ τῇ τοῦ Χριστοῦ δόξῃ καὶ Ἰουδαῖοι, καὶ ἀντιλέγεται διὰ τοῦτο τὸ κατὰ νόμον θυσιαστήριον. Πέπαυται γὰρ ἡ ὡς ἐν σκιαῖς λατρεία· καὶ ἐν Χριστῷ δὴ μᾶλλον εὐωδιάζομεν τῷ Πατρὶ τὴν νοητὴν εὐοσμίαν· καὶ τοῦτο ἡμῖν ὡς ἐν σκιαῖς πάλιν ὑπετύπου, λέγων· «Καὶ ποιήσεις μοι θυσιαστήριον θυμιάματος ἐκ ξύλων ἀσήπτων, καὶ ποιήσεις αὐτὸ πήχεως τὸ μῆκος, καὶ πήχεως τὸ εὖρος· τετράγωνον ἔσται, καὶ δύο πήχεων τὸ ὕψος. Ἐξ αὐτοῦ ἔσται τὰ κέρατα αὐτοῦ, καὶ καταχρυσώσεις αὐτὸ χρυσίῳ καθαρῷ, τὴν ἐσχάραν αὐτοῦ, καὶ τοὺς τοίχους αὐτοῦ κύκλῳ, καὶ τὰ κέρατα αὐτοῦ.» Σκυτάλας δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ κρίκους, καὶ ἀναφορέας, ἕτερά τε τοιαῦτα προστεθεικὼς, καὶ θήσεις αὐτὸ, φησὶν, «Ἔναντι τοῦ καταπε
pass_a_gloss: [Cont. from s.14: Korah, Dathan... running against the vote from above, and] rising up against (κατεξανιστάμενοι) the divine laws, were bringing (προσῆγον) fire-pans (πυρεῖα), uncalled (ἄκλητοι) and self-moved (αὐτόμολοι) going to this, and seizing (ἁρπάζοντες) an honor (τιμή) not allotted (νεμηθεῖσαν) to them, very hotly (θερμῶς) drawing up in opposition (ἀντιπαρεξάγοντες) the things from madness (ἀπόνοια) and boldness (θράσος) against the priest who was preeminent (προὔχοντι) and chosen out selectively (ἀπολέγδην ἐξῃρημένῳ) from all the others. Through these was sketched in shadow (ἐσκιαγραφεῖτο) the coming madness of the Jews against Christ. For he [is] our high priest (ἀρχιερεύς), led to this by the vote from the Father; and those men paid (ἐκτετίκασι) the penalty (δίκας) for such shameful attempts (ἐπιχειρήματα); and after them the Jews will pay, having become liable (ἔνοχοι) to equal charges (ἐγκλήματα). God then said to holy Moses and also to Eleazar the priest from Aaron: [Num 17:2-3 LXX] Take up (ἀνέλεσθε) the bronze fire-pans from the midst of the burned (κεκαυμένων), and this strange (ἀλλότριον) fire scatter (σπεῖρον) there, because he/it sanctified (ἡγίασε) the fire-pans of these sinners in their souls/lives (ἐν ταῖς ψυχαῖς). And they made them beaten plates (λεπίδας ἐλατάς), a covering (περίθεμα) for the altar, because they were offered before the Lord and were sanctified. And they became a sign (σημεῖον) to the sons of Israel. Thus God spoke then. In Exodus it is written about Bezalel, who was from father Uri, of the tribe of Dan, and leader of all skilled craft (εὐτεχνία): [Exod 38:22 LXX] This one made the bronze altar from the bronze fire-pans which belonged to the men who rebelled (καταστασιάσασι) with the congregation (συναγωγή) of Korah. | PALL.: What then is this? | CYR.: It would have much benefit (ὄνησις), if it were considered that the ark was made as a type of Christ, and the others too, lampstand, I say, and the mercy seat (ἱλαστήριον), and the table from gold, the people bringing (προσκομίσαντος) and each dedicating (ἀναθέντος) what was in hand. For very acceptable (δεκτοί) to the glory of God and Father are those bearing fruit (καρποφοροῦντες) to Christ and bringing spiritual (πνευματικάς) gift-offerings (δωροφορίαι), of which [or: of whom] those were types and shadows (σκιαί). But the altar of the worship according to law is signified (σημαίνεται) mystically (μυστικῶς) and economically (οἰκονομικῶς, by the divine plan) as a sort of reminder (ὑπόμνημα) and forewarning proclamation (προαναφώνησις), lying in the very construction, of provocation (παροξυσμός) and contradiction (ἀντιλογία), and so to say, revolt (ἀντάρσις) that happened against the great priest. Is the riddle clear? For Aaron [is] in type of Christ; the Jews contended (πεφιλονεικήκασι) against the glory of Christ, and for this reason the altar according to law is contradicted (ἀντιλέγεται). For the worship as in shadows has ceased (πέπαυται); and in Christ rather we give off fragrance (εὐωδιάζομεν) to the Father, the intelligible (νοητήν) sweet smell (εὐοσμία); and this he prefigured (ὑπετύπου) to us again as in shadows, saying: [Exod 30:1-3] You shall make me an altar of incense (θυμίαμα) from unrotting woods, a cubit length, a cubit breadth; square, two cubits height; from it its horns; and you shall gild (καταχρυσώσεις) it with pure gold, its grate (ἐσχάρα), its walls (τοίχους) around, and its horns. Having added staves (σκυτάλαι), rings (κρίκοι), carrying-poles (ἀναφορεῖς), and other such things, And you shall set it, he says, before the ve[il, καταπέτασμα; cont. s.16]
pass_b_english: Cyril: …rising up against the divine laws, brought firepans uninvited, going to this of their own accord and seizing an honor not assigned to them; and out of madness and audacity they drew up their ranks with great heat against the priest who stood first and had been chosen out from all the others (Numbers 16:1–18). Through these events the madness that the Jews would later show against Christ was sketched in outline. For he himself is our High Priest, brought to this by the decision of the Father. Those men paid the penalty for such shameful attempts, and after them the Jews too will pay it, since they have become liable to the same charges. Then God said to holy Moses, and also to Eleazar the priest, the son of Aaron: ‘Take up the bronze firepans from among those who were burned, and scatter this strange fire there, for the firepans of these sinners have become holy at the cost of their lives. And they made them into hammered plates as a covering for the altar, because they had been offered before the Lord and were made holy. And they became a sign to the sons of Israel.’ (Numbers 16:37–38) This is what God said at that time. And in Exodus it is written about Bezalel, whose father was Uri and whose tribe was Dan, and who led in every kind of skilled craft: ‘He made the bronze altar from the bronze firepans that belonged to the men who rebelled with the company of Korah’ (Exodus 38:22, Septuagint).
Palladius: What, then, does this mean?

Cyril: It would be of great benefit if one considered that the ark was made as a type of Christ, and so too were the other things, I mean the lampstand and the mercy seat and the table of gold, when the people brought their offerings and each one dedicated what he had in hand. For those who bear fruit for Christ and bring spiritual offerings are very acceptable, to the glory of God the Father; and those people of old were types and shadows of them. But the altar of the worship under the law is shown, mystically and by God’s design, to be a kind of memorial and proclamation in advance, lying in its very construction, of the provocation and defiance, and, if I may now put it so, the revolt, that arose against the great priest. Is the riddle clear to you? For Aaron stands as a type of Christ; and the Jews too contended against the glory of Christ, and for this reason the altar under the law is spoken against. For the worship as in shadows has ceased, and in Christ instead we give forth to the Father a spiritual fragrance. And this too he sketched for us beforehand, again as in shadows, when he said: ‘And you shall make for me an altar of incense of wood that does not rot; you shall make it a cubit long and a cubit wide. choices.why: ἐν ταῖς ψυχαῖς αὐτῶν ('in their souls') rendered 'at the cost of their lives', its sense in the Hebrew and LXX.

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of Cyril De adoratione Book 9 exists. Translated fresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the earlier English of this book was not used as a base.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; column may cut mid-sentence.

Opens mid-sentence, completing s.14 (the grammar of the Korah sentence is loose in Greek: dative τοῖς ἀμφ’ αὐτούς with nominative participles; rendered as one subject). The Korah narrative (Korah and Dathan, firepans, seizing the priesthood) is paraphrased from Numbers 16:1–18 and cited there; Abiram is not named. 'Brought to this by the decision of the Father' likely echoes Hebrews 5:4–5; left uncited as not verbal. The firepan command is LXX Numbers 17:2–3 = English Numbers 16:37–38 (LXX 17:1–15 = English 16:36–50). Cyril's text has ἡγίασε (singular) where Rahlfs has ἡγίασαν; read with τὰ πυρεῖα as its neuter-plural subject (singular verb by rule), 'the firepans have become holy', which matches the Hebrew ('for they are holy') and the following ἡγιάσθησαν; reviewer replaced the earlier 'he has hallowed', which supplied an agent the Greek does not name. ἐν ταῖς ψυχαῖς αὐτῶν ('in their souls') rendered 'at the cost of their lives', its sense in the Hebrew and LXX. His text has 'they made them' (ἐποίησαν) where the LXX has the command 'make them' (ποίησον); kept as he quotes it. The verse about Bezalel making the bronze altar from Korah's firepans exists only in the Septuagint (Exodus 38:22 in the LXX, Brenton 38:22; no counterpart in the Hebrew or English Bible, whose bronze altar is Exodus 38:1–7); hence the citation 'Exodus 38:22, Septuagint'. Cyril says Bezalel was of the tribe of Dan; Exodus 31:2 and 38:22 (English) make him of Judah, and Oholiab of Dan (Exodus 31:6). Translated as Cyril wrote it; the slip is his or his text's. 'The people brought their offerings and each dedicated what he had in hand' refers to Exodus 25:1–8 and 35:20–29; left uncited as a general reference. 'Those people of old' renders the masculine ἐκεῖνοι (the Israelite givers); ὧν could also mean the offerings. 'Defiance' (ἀντιλογία, 'speaking against', echoed by ἀντιλέγεται 'is spoken against' just after) may recall Jude 11 ('the rebellion of Korah'); 'we give forth to the Father the spiritual fragrance' may recall 2 Corinthians 2:15; both left uncited as doubtful. νοητός ('perceived by the mind') rendered 'spiritual'. οἰκονομικῶς rendered 'by God's design'. The incense altar's 'grate' (ἐσχάρα) follows the LXX of Exodus 30:3 (Hebrew: its top). The poles, rings and carrying bars summarise Exodus 30:4–5. The quotation of Exodus 30:6–10 begins at the end and continues in s.16, mid-word (καταπε|τάσματος, 'before the | veil'); its citation belongs to s.16.
